earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog bulg1265 lists only Z'graggen 1975 (Madang survey, pp. 8-9, subclassification); no grammar, sketch, or phonology of Bulgebi located.

sources.citation: Carter, Jed, Beautlyn Eliab, Karl Kama, Roger Maikei, Devin O'Bannon & Napa Yanderave. 2023. Survey Report for Uma (Ronji) [roe], Tandɨ (Yagomi) [ygm], Muratayak [asx], Degenang (Degenan) [dge], and Forak [frq] Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2023-003: 1-71. SIL International.
sources.note: Most recent survey of the Warup family (Bulgebi's closest relatives); may report on the Bulgebi/Gamane community and its language status, and its wordlists show the family's phonological profile; not a Bulgebi description.

sources.citation: Carter, John, Katie Carter, John Grummitt, Bonnie MacKenzie & Janell Masters. 2012. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Mur Village Vernaculars. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-043. Dallas: SIL International. 71 pp. (Glottolog ref 311276, listed by Glottolog as a wordlist.)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: nothing on Bulgebi (not named); no stress/tone terms anywhere in the report. Useful negative evidence: as of 2011-12 SIL-PNG's own archive held no Bulgebi wordlist. Also cites Brownie, Hayward & Sweeney 1995 (missed_works 3). Full PDF read in the work dir; only an extract kept in our files because the work does not concern bmp.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid bulg1265 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Only reference: Z'graggen 1975 pp. 8-9 (comments on subclassification). Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology. AES status moribund.

sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content; states that SIL PNG held no processed materials (no survey report, wordlist, data paper or phonology) for Bulgebi as of the 2016 capture. The successor site (pnglanguages.sil.org/resources/search/code/bmp) is could not be reached by automated download and its only Internet Archive copy (2025) could not be reached by automated download pages.

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 2001. Language endangerment in the insular Greater Pacific area, and the New Guinea area in particular. In Andrew Pawley, Malcolm Ross & Darrell Tryon (eds), The boy from Bundaberg: Studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton, 383-397. Pacific Linguistics 514. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: no phonology content: Bulgebi appears only as one row in a list of endangered Papuan languages (status letter, speaker number, province); the words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the chapter.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1975. North-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study 1, 527-567. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any language. Sec. 2.8.1.3.7 Warup Family: 'To these Z'graggen (1973) has added BULGEBI and YAGOMI'; 2.8.1.3.7.2 'Bulgebi (WR-48), pop. 50. Warup Census Division: Bulgebi.' Phonology sec. 2.8.1.4.1 (pp. 544-546) tabulates phonemes and syllable structure of ten representative Finisterre-Huon languages (Kâte, Ono, Selepet, Kube, Nabak, Urii, Wantoat, Kewieng, Rawa, Kovai), none from the Warup family; stress not mentioned.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The Languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. 156 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Classification + village census only. p. 4: 'Short wordlists only were collected in B8 Dumun, A14 Bulgebi, A23 Mebu, M10 Kominimung and M11 Igana; they were however enough for a linguistic classification.' p. 9 (p. 17): 'WARUP FAMILY 3,118.. A14 Bulgebi 52 / Bulgebi 52'. No phonological remark on any Warup language.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, Vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/252971)
sources.note: no phonology content for Bulgebi: the name occurs once, in the map legend ('WARUP FAMILY A7 Yagomi A8 Asat A9 Forak A10 Degenan A11 Morafa A12 Dahating A13 Guiarak A14 Bulgebi'); the words stress, accent and pitch do not occur anywhere in the chapter and 'tone' does not occur as a linguistic term; the body treats classification history, typological features and lexicostatistics of Madang-Adelbert Range languages only.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1973. Some grammatical comparisons of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22. viii+80 pp. (cited by ANU as 'Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages')
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Ch. 1 Phonology (pp. 5-6): phoneme table and syllable structure of the same ten representative languages, no Warup language, no suprasegmental statement. Warup Family listed p. 3 as Degenan, Asat, Morafa, Dahating (Bulgebi not yet named).

sources.citation: Claassen, O. R. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range — New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, Pacific Linguistics A-23, 45-78.
sources.note: Survey/lexicostatistics. Sec. 2.2 Warup Family (pop. 1700) = Asat, Degenan, Morafa; 2.3 Dahating isolate. Bulgebi not mentioned (first identified by Z'graggen). Only stress remark is a footnote on Wantoat: 'Davis (1967) states that stress is non-phonemic' — a different family.
